Question Choices: How many conditions must hold for f to be continuous at x = a? Use an interior point and the standard checklist ordered as value, finite limit, agreement.
Hints: Value, limit, and their agreement.|Count them.
Solution: At an interior point, continuity requires (1) f(a) defined, (2) a finite two-sided limit exists, and (3) that limit equals f(a). A hole with a finite limit can be repaired by assigning its limiting value. On a closed interval [a,b] with a<b, use right continuity at a and left continuity at b. The stated data or matching bounds give 3.

Question Choices: A graph jumps from y = 2 to y = 5 at x = 1. What type of discontinuity is this?
Hints: The one-sided limits differ but are finite.|The graph breaks.
Solution: The notation x->a+ means x>a approaches a; x->a- means x<a approaches a. A finite two-sided limit exists exactly when both one-sided limits exist as the same finite number. Unequal finite one-sided limits give a jump discontinuity, regardless of the function value at a. It is a jump discontinuity.

Question Choices: A graph has a vertical asymptote at x = 4. What type of discontinuity is this?
Hints: The outputs grow without bound.|A vertical asymptote is present.
Solution: An infinite limit describes outputs exceeding every bound in a specified direction; infinity is not a finite real value. At a finite target, inspect the sign of a small denominator on each side. Opposite infinite directions do not give a two-sided infinite limit; matching directions do. At least one infinite one-sided limit establishes a vertical asymptote. It is an infinite discontinuity.
